newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian train accident kills at least eight.
newsitem.headline: Italian train accident kills at least eight.

text.p: At least eight people died on Sunday when a high-speed train hurtled off the track and crashed into electricity pylons in northern Italy.
Police and firemen at the scene said they believed the toll was probably final but could not exclude that more victims were inside the tangled wreckage of the Milan to Rome express.
Security police in Rome issued a statement saying there were no indications that the derailment may have been caused by sabotage, such as obstacles placed on the tracks.
Several politicians had expressed suspicions because former president Francesco Cossiga was on board. He was unhurt and later flew to Rome.
Alberto Grassi, a magistrate involved in the investigation of the derailment, told reporters at the scene "there are no elements to suspect foul play".
Italia Fortunati, prefect (regional governor) of Piacenza, said preliminary indications were that the accident was caused by excessive speed as the train approached a station.
State railways said in a statement eight people had been confirmed dead at 1515 GMT -- nearly three hours after the accident -- and 25 were injured.
The "Pendolino," Italy's fastest train, was derailed as it was approaching the station of Piacenza, about 50 km (30 miles) south of Milan. It had not been due to stop at the station.
Seven of its eight carriages came off the track.
Witnesses said the first was completely ripped open and the sixth still upright but crushed between the fifth and seventh carriages. The train hit a number of pylons before it came to a halt.
"The train was going very fast and all of a sudden we found ourselves lying sideways. It was terrible," a member of the crew told Italian radio.
The victims had not been formally identified but they were all believed to be Italian.
A railway official at the scene said the dead were belived to be two conductors, an on-board hostess, three railway police and two other passengers.
The accident blocked rail traffic in both directions on the main north-south link.
The railways statement said trains to and from northern Italy were being re-routed via other cities.
The accident came less than two weeks after four people were killed in a train accident near the northern city of Brescia.
